note: Adapted from the species description of Chhotani (1997), originally in English; the alate is unknown, and both the soldier and the worker are described; synonymy citations, distribution records and figure numbers are not translated.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule straw yellow; base of nasus light brown, darker distally; antennae slightly tinged with light brown, darker than head; pronotum pale yellow, darker anteriorly; abdomen yellowish white. Head covered with minute hairs, with a pair of longer setae on vertex and another at base of nasus; each abdominal tergite with one long seta on each side, the last few tergites with more long hairs; sternites densely covered with long and short hairs. Body length 4.0–5.2 mm. Head capsule subcircular, wider than long (1.75–1.98 mm long including nasus, 1.10–1.20 mm long excluding nasus, 1.20–1.38 mm maximum width); in lateral view distinctly incurved behind nasus, without nasus swelling; posterior margin rounded, sometimes slightly emarginate at middle; sides rounded and strongly convex. Nasus conical, very thick at base (0.60–0.80 mm long, nasus length/head length index 0.52–0.65). Antennae 12–13-segmented; segment 3 about one and a half times segment 2. Mandibles vestigial, without spine-like processes or with only extremely minute ones. Pronotum saddle-shaped, with several minute hairs and a few long hairs (0.20–0.31 mm long, 0.48–0.60 mm wide); anterior margin without notch.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule smoky brown; frons and postclypeus yellowish white; antennae and labrum straw yellow; pronotum light brown. Body length 3.5–5.0 mm. Head capsule subquadrate and rounded (0.80–1.20 mm long to base of mandibles, 1.05–1.30 mm maximum width); coronal suture weak to distinct. Fontanelle plate long, nearly white. Antennae 14-segmented; segment 3 shorter than segment 2, equal in length to segment 4. Postclypeus inflated, hairy; less than 1/2 as long as wide. Pronotum saddle-shaped (0.18–0.35 mm long, 0.48–0.65 mm wide); anterior margin distinctly notched.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The soldier mandibles bear extremely minute spine-like processes that break off easily; the statement in the literature that the outer margin has no spine-like process may result from the spines having been lost in the specimens examined.
